text: For Heidegger, the present-at-hand (theoretical, object-directed) mode of encountering things is derivative, emerging when smooth ready-to-hand engagement breaks down.
explanation: True. Heidegger holds that the present-at-hand mode is derivative, arising when absorbed ready-to-hand coping is disrupted (the tool breaks or goes missing); the detached, contemplative subject confronting objects is a secondary rather than fundamental mode.
